Identify primary evidence that changes these maps; verify identity/population and exact accessible supporting/qualifying/null passages; recommend atomic changes vs out-of-scope/no-change/access-insufficient. Priorities: MN NELL1/PLA2R complement DOI10.1111/nep.70288; Behcet SPHK1 DOI10.3389/fimmu.2026.1764448 (murineBMDM/humanblood) and IRF8 DOI10.18632/oncotarget.17235 (PMIDs28472775/28881647); IgG4 ocularfibrosis100cases and ageing lesion transcriptomics; CREST TTLL7-IT1/miR29c/GLS DOI10.3389/fimmu.2026.1722661 and mosaic alterations DOI10.1016/j.ard.2026.06.006; MCD exosomes DOI10.1016/j.jare.2026.01.032 and AA/PKM2 DOI10.1111/jcmm.71404; FSGS PDGF-C DOI10.1681/asn.0000001274; Sjogren CD4-adoptive-transfer/meibomian gland and B-cell-therapy transcriptomic nonresponse. Include negatives. Independently re-review calciphylaxis PPi interpretation: lowerPPi associated with disease/mortality,30matchedpairs/70cohort,67%ESKD,no painassociation,observational,industryfunded,noPPiintervention. Earlier abstract-only reviewer could not verify counts/variability; exact citable primaryfulltext excerpts follow. Return consistent_with_caveats/needs_revision/insufficient_evidence for PPi. Disclose actual searches/access limits. Do not claim screening our5884localrecords; we screen locally. No library changes.

crest-syndrome: A bounded limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis map: anticentromere autoimmunity, endothelial vasculopathy with a pulmonary arterial hypertension branch, fibroblast activation and calcinosis [scope abbreviated]
diffuse-systemic-sclerosis: Diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis: autoimmunity, endothelial injury, fibroblast activation and skin fibrosis, with interstitial lung disease and renal crisis branches. Mixed- [scope abbreviated]

Exact full-text PPi RESULTS (PMC13571338, DOI10.1016/j.jacadv.2026.103205):
At enrollment, for the entire calciphylaxis cohort (n = 70), the median age was 60 years (IQR: 53-70). Cohort was predominantly comprised of females (69%) and Caucasian race (71%). Comorbidities included ESKD (67%), diabetes (78%), coronary artery disease (44%) with a median body mass index (BMI) of 31 kg/m2 (IQR: 27-37), and 37% on warfarin. Serum calcium and phosphorous were mostly unremarkable. The median intact parathyroid hormone and alkaline phosphatase (ALP) were elevated (median intact parathyroid hormone: 130 pg/mL, IQR: 42-252; median ALP: 123 IU/L, IQR: 89-192) compared to reference ranges. The median skin lesion count was 3 (IQR: 2-4) and median pain intensity was 5 (IQR: 4-7) on a 0 to 10 scale. Mortality was 21% (15 dead, 55 alive) by 6-week and 27% (19 dead, 51 alive) by 12-week follow-up. Deaths were caused by either sepsis originating from wound infection or withdrawal from dialysis due to disease burden.
For case-control analysis, patient characteristics were well-balanced between cases (n = 30) and matched controls (n = 30), except for serum ALP which was higher in cases (median: 132 IU/L; IQR: 102-214) than in controls (median: 99 IU/L; IQR: 75-147, P = 0.03). ESKD was present in 67% of cases and controls (Table 1). PPi levels were significantly lower among patients with calciphylaxis compared to matched controls, (cases: median: 248 nM, [IQR: 110-323]; controls: median: 611 nM, [IQR: 361-799]; P < 0.001). The finding of lower PPi levels in calciphylaxis compared to controls was consistent in analyses stratified by presence or absence of ESKD. Moreover, PPi levels in patients with calciphylaxis were substantially lower than those previously reported for healthy adults by Khursigara et al5 (median: 2,167 nM [IQR: 1,787-2,969]). In conditional logistic regression model adjusted for ALP, phosphate, and BMI, each 100 nM reduction in PPi was associated with a 68% higher odds of calciphylaxis (OR: 1.68, 95% CI: 1.26-2.42).
At enrollment, PPi levels negatively correlated with the number of skin lesions (rs = −0.26; P = 0.03) but not with pain intensity. Compared to calciphylaxis patients who were alive by 6 weeks, those who died had significantly lower enrollment PPi levels (245 nM [IQR: 78-543] vs 727 nM [IQR: 341-1,232], P = 0.002). Among ESKD patients with calciphylaxis, each 100 nM reduction in enrollment PPi was associated with ∼50% higher 6-week mortality after adjusting for age, sex, and BMI (OR: 1.54; 95% CI: 1.09-2.18). A similar association was also noted between enrollment PPi and 12-week mortality. There was a substantial within-individual variability between 6-week and enrollment PPi levels.

render_instructions: 1. FIRST, before any other output, reproduce message_for_user verbatim so the user gets the Consensus link immediately. The anchor text must be exactly 'View this in Consensus' — never hyperlink the thread title, a paper title, or any other phrase.

2. When status='idle', write the interaction's `document` field to the file named in the top-level `filename` field (already sanitized for filesystem use), or render it in the client's artifact, canvas, drawer, or side-panel surface. `document` is already a complete markdown document with a References footer — write it out byte-for-byte. Do NOT paste the analysis inline into chat.

3. CRITICAL: every inline citation marker MUST survive into whatever you render. Never drop, renumber, merge, or convert them to prose. Output without the markers is incorrect. [N.M] cites quote M from paper N, and the References footer lists that quote under paper N's entry with the same [N.M] label (a bare [N] cites paper N without a quote). Do not paraphrase, summarize, or rewrite `document` or `response` — copy them verbatim. Each inline marker in `response` and `document` is already hyperlinked to its paper (the References labels are plain text); preserve those links.

4. If you build the output yourself instead of using `document`, use `response` verbatim as the body and append a '## References' section listing every entry of citations[] with its n, title, authors, year, journal, doi, url, institutional_access_url (when present, as an 'Access through your institution' link), and every snippet's marker, quote, and section.
5. In chat, output only a 2-3 sentence summary plus the Consensus link. The full analysis belongs in the file or artifact.

6. Evidence-strength scores, top authors, the results timeline, the research-gap matrix, and the search funnel are already written into `response` and `document` as text and tables; keep them as they are. The consensus meter and citation graph are interactive visuals that exist ONLY in the Consensus UI: point the user at `url` for them.
schema_note: Full research thread. Top level: thread_id, title, status ('idle'/'running'/'failed'), url (Consensus deep-link), filename (sanitized output basename), message_for_user, display_first, interactions[]. Each interaction mirrors the persisted thread row: interaction_id, input_message, created_at, search_mode, mode, status, filters, full_text_paper_ids, response (cleaned markdown whose inline [N.M] markers, quote M of paper N, are hyperlinked to the cited paper; a bare [N] cites a paper without a quote), document (ready-to-write markdown file: response, a Consensus disclaimer and a References footer), citations[] (hydrated paper metadata and paper urls, plus institutional_access_url, the paper's full text through the user's institution, when they have one; each grounding snippet carries the marker that cites it), cited_papers[] (rank -> paper_id, where rank is citations[].n: papers are numbered in order of first citation in response, not by search rank), stats (retrieved/eligible/included counts), step_count (number of visible registered trace nodes), agent_trace (text summary), and agent_trace_raw (full graph nodes, only if include_trace=true).
